### Basic Zod Schema Definition and Validation

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/index.mdx

This example demonstrates how to define a basic Zod object schema, parse untrusted input data, and access the type-safe result.

```ts
import * as z from "zod";

const User = z.object({
  name: z.string(),
});

// some untrusted data...
const input = { /* stuff */ };

// the parsed result is validated and type safe!
const data = User.parse(input);

// so you can use it with confidence :)
console.log(data.name);
```

--------------------------------

### Differentiating Zod 3 and Zod 4 schemas at runtime

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/library-authors.mdx

Code example showing how to check for the `_zod` property to determine if a schema is Zod 3 or Zod 4.

```ts
import type * as z3 from "zod/v3";
import type * as z4 from "zod/v4/core";

declare const schema: z3.ZodTypeAny | z4.$ZodType;

if ("_zod" in schema) {
  schema._zod.def; // Zod 4 schema
} else {
  schema._def; // Zod 3 schema
}
```

--------------------------------

### Interleaving transformations and refinements

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs-v3/MIGRATION.md

Demonstrates how transformations and refinements can be interleaved using the dedicated 'ZodEffects' class.

```typescript
const test = z
    .string()
    .transform((val) => val.length)
    .refine((val) => val > 5, { message: "Input is too short" })
    .transform((val) => val * 2);

test.parse("12characters"); // => 24
```

### User code demonstrating Zod and Zod Mini usage

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/library-authors.mdx

Example of user code calling a library function with schemas from both Zod and Zod Mini, showing simultaneous support.

```ts
// user code
import { acceptObjectSchema } from "your-library";

// Zod 4
import * as z from "zod";
acceptObjectSchema(z.object({ name: z.string() }));

// Zod 4 Mini
import * as zm from "zod/mini";
acceptObjectSchema(zm.object({ name: zm.string() }))
```

### Traversing Zod Schemas

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/packages/core.mdx

Example of how to traverse Zod schemas using the `_zod.def` property to discriminate between types.

```ts
export function walk(_schema: z.$ZodType) {
  const schema = _schema as z.$ZodTypes;
  const def = schema._zod.def;
  switch (def.type) {
    case "string": {
      // ...
      break;
    }
    case "object": {
      // ...
      break;
    }
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Demonstrate TypeScript Structural Typing

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs-v3/home.md

This example illustrates TypeScript's structural typing, where types with identical structures are considered compatible, even if nominally different.

```ts
type Cat = { name: string };
type Dog = { name: string };

const petCat = (cat: Cat) => {};
const fido: Dog = { name: "fido" };
petCat(fido); // works fine
```

--------------------------------

### Registering, looking up, and removing schemas

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/metadata.mdx

Shows how to add, check for, get, remove, and clear schemas in a registry.

```ts
const mySchema = z.string();

myRegistry.add(mySchema, { description: "A cool schema!"});
myRegistry.has(mySchema); // => true
myRegistry.get(mySchema); // => { description: "A cool schema!" }
myRegistry.remove(mySchema);
myRegistry.clear(); // wipe registry
```

### Library code for Zod and Zod Mini compatibility

// library code
import * as z4 from "zod/v4/core";

export function acceptObjectSchema<T extends z4.$ZodObject>(schema: T){
  // parse data
  z4.parse(schema, { /* somedata */});
  // inspect internals
  schema._zod.def.shape;
}
```

--------------------------------

### Static type vs runtime divergence examples

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/wiki/optionality.md

Illustrates the difference between Zod's static type inference and its runtime behavior, especially with `catch` and `preprocess`.

```typescript
z.input<typeof z.object({ a: z.string().catch("c") })>
// → { a: string }   — `a` is required at the type level

z.object({ a: z.string().catch("c") }).parse({})
// → { a: "c" }      — but accepts {} at runtime

z.input<typeof z.object({ a: z.preprocess(fn, T) })>
// → { a: <transform's input type> }   — `a` is required at the type level

z.object({ a: z.preprocess(fn, T) }).parse({})
// → { a: fn(undefined) }   — accepts {} at runtime
```

--------------------------------

### Constraining the inferred output type of the input schema

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/library-authors.mdx

Example of how to constrain the inferred output type of the input schema, ensuring type compatibility.

```ts

import * as z4 from "zod/v4/core";

// only accepts string schemas
function inferSchema<T extends z4.$ZodType<string>>(schema: T) {
  return schema;
}

inferSchema(z.string()); // ✅ 

inferSchema(z.number()); 
// ❌ The types of '_zod.output' are incompatible between these types. 
// // Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'string'
```

--------------------------------

### `json(schema)` Usage Example

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/codecs.mdx

Demonstrates how to use the `jsonCodec` with a specific Zod schema to decode JSON strings into objects and encode objects back into JSON strings, including error handling for invalid input.

```ts
const jsonToObject = jsonCodec(z.object({ name: z.string(), age: z.number() }));

jsonToObject.decode('{"name":"Alice","age":30}');  
// => { name: "Alice", age: 30 }

jsonToObject.encode({ name: "Bob", age: 25 });     
// => '{"name":"Bob","age":25}'

jsonToObject.decode('~~invalid~~'); 
// ZodError: [
//   {
//     "code": "invalid_format",
//     "format": "json",
//     "path": [],
//     "message": "Unexpected token '~', \"~~invalid~~\" is not valid JSON"
//   }
// ]
```

### Async Codec Definition

Example of defining an asynchronous codec with `decode` and `encode` functions that return Promises.

```ts
const asyncCodec = z.codec(z.string(), z.number(), {
  decode: async (str) => Number(str),
  encode: async (num) => num.toString()
});
```

### Inverting a Codec

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/codecs.mdx

Example of using `z.invertCodec()` to create a codec that reverses the input and output schemas and transformations.

```typescript
const dateToString = z.invertCodec(stringToDate);

dateToString.decode(new Date("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"));
// => string

dateToString.encode("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z");
// => Date
```

```typescript
const dateToString = z.invertCodec(stringToDate);

z.decode(dateToString, new Date("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"));
// => string

z.encode(dateToString, "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z");
// => Date
```

### Defining a Codec

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/codecs.mdx

Example of defining a codec to transform an ISO date string to a Date object and vice-versa.

```typescript
const stringToDate = z.codec(
  z.iso.datetime(),  // input schema: ISO date string
  z.date(),          // output schema: Date object
  {
    decode: (isoString) => new Date(isoString), // ISO string → Date
    encode: (date) => date.toISOString(),       // Date → ISO string
  }
);
```

### Parsing data with Zod Core functions

```ts
function parseData<T extends z4.$ZodType>(data: unknown, schema: T): z4.output<T> {
  return z.parse(schema, data);
}

parseData("sup", z.string());
// => string
```

{
  formErrors: [ 'Unrecognized key: "extraKey"' ],
  fieldErrors: {

### Handling errors with .safeParse()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/basics.mdx

Using .safeParse() to get a result object instead of throwing an error.

```ts
const result = Player.safeParse({ username: 42, xp: "100" });
if (!result.success) {
  result.error;   // ZodError instance
} else {
  result.data;    // { username: string; xp: number }
}
```

### z.url([options])

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Creates a schema to validate strings against WHATWG URL standards using the JavaScript URL constructor. Options allow matching hostnames, protocols, and normalizing URL values.

```APIDOC
## z.url([options])

### Description
Validates WHATWG-compatible URLs across JavaScript runtimes using the `new URL()` constructor. Options allow constraining the protocol, hostname, or enabling URL normalization.

### Signature
`z.url(options?: { hostname?: RegExp; protocol?: RegExp; normalize?: boolean })`

### Related Methods
- `z.httpUrl()` - Restricts protocol to `http`/`https` and hostname to `z.regexes.domain`

### Parameters
- **hostname** (`RegExp`, optional) - Regular expression pattern to validate the URL hostname
- **protocol** (`RegExp`, optional) - Regular expression pattern to validate the URL protocol
- **normalize** (`boolean`, optional) - When true, normalizes input value with the URL returned by `new URL().href`

### Usage Example
```ts
const schema = z.url();
schema.parse("https://example.com"); // passes
schema.parse("mailto:noreply@zod.dev"); // passes

// With hostname/protocol constraints
z.url({ hostname: /^example\.com$/ });
z.url({ protocol: /^https$/ });

// Web URLs only
z.httpUrl();
```
```

--------------------------------

### z.input(schema)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Runtime counterpart to z.input<T> that replaces every pipe in a schema with its input side.

```APIDOC
## z.input(schema)

### Description
Runtime counterpart to the type-level `z.input<T>`. Replaces every pipe in a schema with its input side. Useful for reaching codecs nested inside objects, records, or maps.

### Signature
- `z.input(schema: ZodSchema): ZodSchema`

### Parameters
- `schema` (ZodSchema) - The schema containing pipes/codecs to extract input validation from.

### Usage Example
```ts
const Event = z.object({ name: z.string(), at: stringToDate });

z.input(Event).parse({ name: "launch", at: "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" }); // ✅
```
```

### z.output(schema)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Runtime counterpart to z.output<T> that replaces every pipe in a schema with its output side.

```APIDOC
## z.output(schema)

### Description
Runtime counterpart to the type-level `z.output<T>`. Replaces every pipe in a schema with its output side. Note that calling `z.output()` on a one-way transform returns the transform itself.

### Signature
- `z.output(schema: ZodSchema): ZodSchema`

### Parameters
- `schema` (ZodSchema) - The schema containing pipes/codecs to extract output validation from.

### Usage Example
```ts
const Event = z.object({ name: z.string(), at: stringToDate });

z.output(Event).parse({ name: "launch", at: new Date() }); // ✅
```
```

### refine(fn, options) - when parameter

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Allows fine-grained control over when a refinement runs. By default, refinements do not run if non-continuable issues exist, but the when parameter allows defining custom execution conditions.

```APIDOC
## refine(fn, options)

### Description
Defines a custom refinement check on a schema, with optional execution control via the `when` option.

### Parameters
- **fn** `(data: T) => boolean | Promise<boolean>` - The refinement validation function returning `true` if valid or `false` if invalid.
- **options** `object` (optional) - Configuration options for the refinement.
  - **message** `string` (optional) - Custom error message.
  - **path** `(string | number)[]` (optional) - Array specifying the error path.
  - **when** `(payload: { value: unknown, issues: Issue[] }) => boolean` (optional) - Function that returns whether the refinement check should run based on the validation payload and collected issues.

### Usage Example
```ts
const baseSchema = z.object({
  password: z.string().min(8),
  confirmPassword: z.string(),
  anotherField: z.string(),
});

const schema = baseSchema.refine(
  (data) => data.password === data.confirmPassword,
  {
    message: "Passwords do not match",
    path: ["confirmPassword"],
    when(payload) {
      return baseSchema
        .pick({ password: true, confirmPassword: true })
        .safeParse(payload.value).success;
    },
  }
);
```
```

--------------------------------

### Discriminating String Format Checks

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/packages/core.mdx

Example of using a nested switch statement to discriminate between different string format checks.

```ts
const check = {} as z.$ZodChecks;
const def = check._zod.def;

switch (def.check) {
  case "less_than":
  case "greater_than":
  // ...
  case "string_format":
    {
      const formatCheck = check as z.$ZodStringFormatChecks;
      const formatCheckDef = formatCheck._zod.def;

      switch (formatCheckDef.format) {
        case "email":
        case "url":
          // do stuff
      }
    }
    break;
}
```

--------------------------------

### Constraining input schema to a specific subclass

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/library-authors.mdx

Example of how to constrain the accepted schema type to a specific Zod subclass, such as `ZodObject`.

```ts

import * as z4 from "zod/v4/core";

// only accepts object schemas
function inferSchema<T extends z4.$ZodObject>(schema: T) {
  return schema;
}
```

### Regular Zod vs. Zod Mini Chained Methods

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/packages/mini.mdx

Comparison of method chaining in regular Zod versus functional checks in Zod Mini.

```ts
// regular Zod
z.string().min(5).max(10).trim()

// Zod Mini
z.string().check(z.minLength(5), z.maxLength(10), z.trim());
```

### Using a Codec for Decoding and Encoding

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/codecs.mdx

Demonstrates how `decode` and `encode` behave differently when using a codec that diverges input and output types.

```typescript
stringToDate.decode("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z")
// => Date

stringToDate.encode(new Date("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"))
// => string
```

```typescript
z.decode(stringToDate, "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z")
// => Date

z.encode(stringToDate, new Date("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"))
// => string
```

### Basic Zod Schema and Parsing

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/README.md

Demonstrates defining a simple Zod object schema and parsing untrusted data to get a validated, type-safe result.

```typescript
import * as z from "zod";

const User = z.object({
  name: z.string()
});

// some untrusted data...
const input = {
  /* stuff */
};

// the parsed result is validated and type safe!
const data = User.parse(input);

// so you can use it with confidence :)
console.log(data.name);
```

### Implement Dark Theme Toggling with System Preference

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs-v3/index.html

This JavaScript code provides functions to check and toggle the dark theme based on the user's system preferences. It applies the 'dark' class to the body and sets a 'data-theme' attribute on the document's root element.

```javascript
localStorage.removeItem("dark-theme");
function checkDark() {
  return (
    // localStorage.getItem("dark-theme") === "true" ??
    window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches ?? false
  );
}
let isDark = checkDark();
toggleDarkTheme(isDark);
window
  .matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)")
  .addEventListener("change", (e) => toggleDarkTheme(e.matches()));
// document.querySelector(".theme-btn").addEventListener("click", () => {
//   const isDark = checkDark();
//   console.log("isDark", isDark);
//   toggleDarkTheme(!isDark);
// });
function toggleDarkTheme(isDark) {
  if (isDark) {
    document.body.classList.add("dark");
  } else {
    document.body.classList.remove("dark");
  }
  document.documentElement.setAttribute(
    "data-theme",
    isDark ? "dark" : "light"
  );
  // localStorage.setItem("dark-theme", isDark ? "true" : "false");
}
```

### Interleave Zod Transforms and Refinements

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs-v3/home.md

Chain `.transform()` and `.refine()` methods to first modify data and then validate the transformed value. This example transforms a string to its length, then refines based on that length.

```ts
z.string()
  .transform((val) => val.length)
  .refine((val) => val > 25);
```

### Example ZodError Issues

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs-v3/ERROR_HANDLING.md

```ts
[
  {
    code: "invalid_type",
    expected: "string",
    received: "number",
    path: ["names", 1],
    message: "Invalid input: expected string, received number",
  },
  {
    code: "unrecognized_keys",
    keys: ["extra"],
    path: ["address"],
    message: "Unrecognized key(s) in object: 'extra'",
  },
  {
    code: "too_small",
    minimum: 10000,
    type: "number",
    inclusive: true,
    path: ["address", "zipCode"],
    message: "Value should be greater than or equal to 10000",

];

### Apply size constraints to Set schemas in Zod and Zod Mini

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Restricts set sizes using utility methods or check helpers for minimum, maximum, and exact item counts.

```ts
z.set(z.string()).nonempty(); // must contain at least 1 item
z.set(z.string()).min(5); // must contain 5 or more items
z.set(z.string()).max(5); // must contain 5 or fewer items
z.set(z.string()).size(5); // must contain 5 items exactly
```

```ts
z.set(z.string()).check(z.minSize(1)); // alias for .nonempty()
z.set(z.string()).check(z.minSize(5)); // must contain 5 or more items
z.set(z.string()).check(z.maxSize(5)); // must contain 5 or fewer items
z.set(z.string()).check(z.size(5)); // must contain 5 items exactly
```

--------------------------------

### z.file()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Creates a schema to validate File instances. Supports constraints on file size and MIME types.

```APIDOC
## z.file()

### Description
Defines a schema for validating `File` instances, allowing configuration of minimum/maximum byte size and allowed MIME types.

### Signature
`z.file() => ZodFile`

### Methods / Constraints
- **.min(bytes: number)** - Minimum `.size` in bytes.
- **.max(bytes: number)** - Maximum `.size` in bytes.
- **.mime(type: string | string[])** - Allowed MIME type or array of MIME types.

### Zod Mini Checks
- **z.minSize(bytes: number)** - Used with `.check(z.minSize(...))`
- **z.maxSize(bytes: number)** - Used with `.check(z.maxSize(...))`
- **z.mime(type: string | string[])** - Used with `.check(z.mime(...))`

### Example (Zod)
```ts
const fileSchema = z.file();

fileSchema.min(10_000); // minimum .size (bytes)
fileSchema.max(1_000_000); // maximum .size (bytes)
fileSchema.mime("image/png"); // MIME type
fileSchema.mime(["image/png", "image/jpeg"]); // multiple MIME types
```

### Example (Zod Mini)
```ts
const fileSchema = z.file();

fileSchema.check(z.minSize(10_000)); // minimum .size (bytes)
fileSchema.check(z.maxSize(1_000_000)); // maximum .size (bytes)
fileSchema.check(z.mime("image/png")); // MIME type
fileSchema.check(z.mime(["image/png", "image/jpeg"])); // multiple MIME types
```
```

--------------------------------

### Public API workarounds for absent-key rejection

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/wiki/optionality.md

Examples demonstrating how to allow absence or provide default values for schemas that are intentionally strict, using `.optional()`, `.default()`, and `.preprocess()`.

```typescript
// Want absence to be allowed on coerce? Wrap in optional:
z.object({ a: z.coerce.string().optional() }).parse({})
// 

// Want absence to map to a default?
z.object({ a: z.coerce.string().default("x") }).parse({})
// { a: "x" }

// Want preprocess to fire on absent inner-required schemas? Use inner-optional:
z.object({ a: z.preprocess(fn, z.string().optional()) }).parse({})
// {}  (or { a: fn(undefined) } if fn returns a defined value 


```

--------------------------------

### React Form with Zod Error Display

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs-v3/ERROR_HANDLING.md

A React example demonstrating how to integrate Zod's `.format()` output to display validation errors next to form fields.

```tsx
const FormData = z.object({ ... });

function Errors(props: {errors?: string[]}){
  if(!props.errors?.length) return null;
  return <div>{props.errors.map(err => <p>{err}</p>)}</div>
}

function MyForm(){
  const {register, data} = useForm({ ... });

  const result = FormData.safeParse(data);
  const errors = result.success ? {} : result.error.format();

  return <div>
    <label>Name<label>
    <input {...register('name')}>
    <Errors errors={errors?.name?._errors} />
  </div>
}
```

### z.uuid([options])

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Creates a schema to validate RFC 9562/4122 UUID strings with optional version targeting. Additional helper constructors are provided for specific UUID versions and general GUID validation.

```APIDOC
## z.uuid([options])

### Description
Validates standard RFC 9562/4122 UUID identifiers. Allows constraining validation to a specific UUID version, or using dedicated shorthand methods and `z.guid()` for general UUID-like identifiers.

### Signature
`z.uuid(options?: { version?: "v1" | "v2" | "v3" | "v4" | "v5" | "v6" | "v7" | "v8" })`

### Related Methods
- `z.uuidv4()` - Shorthand for validating UUID v4
- `z.uuidv6()` - Shorthand for validating UUID v6
- `z.uuidv7()` - Shorthand for validating UUID v7
- `z.guid()` - Validates any UUID-like identifier without the byte 8 bit constraint

### Usage Example
```ts
z.uuid();
z.uuid({ version: "v4" });

z.uuidv4();
z.uuidv6();
z.uuidv7();
z.guid();
```
```

--------------------------------

### Inferring input and output types

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/basics.mdx

Extracting distinct input and output types for schemas with transformations.

```ts
const mySchema = z.string().transform((val) => val.length);

type MySchemaIn = z.input<typeof mySchema>;
// => string

type MySchemaOut = z.output<typeof mySchema>; // equivalent to z.infer<typeof mySchema>
// number
```

### Define a Recursive Category Schema (TypeScript)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs-v3/home.md

Defines a self-referencing schema for categories with subcategories using z.lazy and a manual type hint due to TypeScript limitations. Includes an example of parsing valid data.

```ts
const baseCategorySchema = z.object({
  name: z.string(),
});

type Category = z.infer<typeof baseCategorySchema> & {
  subcategories: Category[];
};

const categorySchema: z.ZodType<Category> = baseCategorySchema.extend({
  subcategories: z.lazy(() => categorySchema.array()),
});

categorySchema.parse({
  name: "People",
  subcategories: [
    {
      name: "Politicians",
      subcategories: [
        {
          name: "Presidents",
          subcategories: [],
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}); // passes
```

### Incorrect Zod Enum Definition without `as const`

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs-v3/home.md

This example shows an incorrect way to define a Zod enum using a mutable array, as Zod cannot infer the exact literal values, leading to a type error.

```ts
const fish = ["Salmon", "Tuna", "Trout"];
const FishEnum = z.enum(fish);
```

--------------------------------

### Execute multiple continuable refinements in Zod and Zod Mini

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Runs all refinement checks in sequence and collects all resulting issues.

```ts
const myString = z.string()
  .refine((val) => val.length > 8, { error: "Too short!" })
  .refine((val) => val === val.toLowerCase(), { error: "Must be lowercase" });
  

const result = myString.safeParse("OH NO");
result.error?.issues;
/* [
  { "code": "custom", "message": "Too short!" },
  { "code": "custom", "message": "Must be lowercase" }
] */
```

```ts
const myString = z.string().check(
  z.refine((val) => val.length > 8, { error: "Too short!" }),
  z.refine((val) => val === val.toLowerCase(), { error: "Must be lowercase" })
);

const result = z.safeParse(myString, "OH NO");
result.error?.issues;
/* [
  { "code": "custom", "message": "Too short!" },
  { "code": "custom", "message": "Must be lowercase" }
] */
```

### .pick()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Creates a new object schema containing only the specified keys from the original schema.

```APIDOC
### Method: `.pick()` / `z.pick()`

#### Description
Extracts a subset of properties from an object schema based on the provided key mask.

#### Signatures
- `schema.pick(keys)` (Zod)
- `z.pick(schema, keys)` (Zod Mini)

#### Parameters
- **keys** (Record<string, true>) - An object with keys to retain set to `true`.

#### Example
```ts
const Recipe = z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  description: z.string().optional(),
  ingredients: z.array(z.string()),
});

const JustTheTitle = Recipe.pick({ title: true });
```
```

--------------------------------

### .catchall(schema)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Specifies a catchall schema used to validate any unrecognized keys found on an object schema.

```APIDOC
### Signature
- Zod: `objectSchema.catchall(schema: ZodTypeAny): ZodObject`
- Zod Mini: `z.catchall(schema: ZodObject, catchallSchema: ZodTypeAny): ZodObject`

### Parameters
- **schema** (`ZodTypeAny`) - Schema used to validate any unrecognized keys.

### Description
Defines a catchall schema on an object schema. Any unrecognized keys present during validation are evaluated against the catchall schema instead of being stripped.

### Usage Example
```ts
// Zod
const DogWithStrings = z
  .object({
    name: z.string(),
    age: z.number().optional(),
  })
  .catchall(z.string());

DogWithStrings.parse({ name: "Yeller", extraKey: "extraValue" }); // ✅
DogWithStrings.parse({ name: "Yeller", extraKey: 42 }); // ❌
```
```

--------------------------------

### z.any() / z.unknown()

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Creates schemas representing TypeScript's any and unknown types to allow any input values.

```APIDOC
### Functions
`z.any()`
`z.unknown()`

### Description
Creates schemas that allow any value, matching TypeScript's `any` and `unknown` types. When used as object properties, keys are required by default.

### Usage
```ts
// allows any values
z.any(); // inferred type: `any`
z.unknown(); // inferred type: `unknown`

z.object({ a: z.any() }).parse({}); // ❌
z.object({ a: z.any() }).parse({ a: undefined }); // ✅
z.object({ a: z.any().optional() }).parse({}); // ✅
```
```

--------------------------------

### codec.parse(input)

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx

Executes the forward transformation by running the codec's decode function on an input value. Accepts unknown input types.

```APIDOC
## `codec.parse(input)`

### Description
Performs the forward transformation using the codec's `decode` function. Accepts `unknown` input and validates it against the input schema before decoding.

### Parameters
- **input** (`unknown`) - Required. The raw input data to parse and decode.

### Return Value
Returns the decoded output matching the output schema type.

### Example
```ts
stringToDate.parse("2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"); // => Date
```
```

--------------------------------

### Refinements with Encoding

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/codecs.mdx

Shows how `.refine()` checks are executed during the encoding process, including how Zod handles errors from refinement logic.

```ts
const schema = stringToDate.refine((date) => date.getFullYear() >= 2000, "Must be this millennium");

schema.encode(new Date("2000-01-01"));
// => Date

schema.encode(new Date("1999-01-01"));
// => 
//   {
//     "code": "custom",
//     "path": [],
//     "message": "Must be this millennium"
//   }
// ]
```

### Validate unknown keys with a catchall schema

Source: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs-v3/home.md

Configures an object schema with `.catchall()` to validate all unrecognized keys against a specified schema, allowing or failing based on the catchall type.

```ts
const person = z
  .object({
    name: z.string(),
  })
  .catchall(z.number());

person.parse({
  name: "bob dylan",
  validExtraKey: 61, // works fine
});

person.parse({
  name: "bob dylan",
  validExtraKey: false, // fails
});
// => throws ZodError
```
